newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine delays privatisation certificate deadline.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine delays privatisation certificate deadline.

text.p: Ukraine's parliament voted on Friday to extend again the deadline for citizens to collect privatisation certificates, with which people can invest in companies being sold off.
The deadline for collecting the certificates was extended to January 1, 1997, from October 1. The authorities started issuing them in January 1995.

In June, the last time the deadline was extended, one third of Ukrainians had not yet picked up their certificates, but more up-to-date figures on how many of the 52 million certificates are still to be collected are not available.
Each Ukrainian can invest the certificates, worth 500 hryvnia ($275), in a single company on a long list of state enterprises which are being privatised.
The certificates can also be sold, without losing their investment rights.
It has not yet been decided how many shares in each company a certificate will be worth.
The transfer of certificates for shares will only begin when all certificates have been collected, or the government no longer extends the deadline.
Part of the problem is that people can only collect their certificates in the locality where they are officially registered, and many have since moved.
Parliament also voted 229-34 to support the State Property Fund in privatising thousands of enterprises still in state hands, and to keep fund chairman Yuri Yekhanurov in his job.
Some deputies in the communist-dominated parliament wanted to remove Yekhanurov for violating laws in the process of privatising state-owned properties.

The deputies charged that the fund had not safeguarded social and economic needs while privatising enterprises, and did not make enough effort to improve the investment climate as Ukraine restructures its economy. -- Irene Marushko, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
